# app_id: # Steam's catalogue as IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1 reported it on 2026-09-26, AS SEEN FROM
# CA, PL, ZA, IL, IN, JP, AU, BR. The countries are not incidental: Steam sells a different catalogue in each,
# from 188,169 games in CA down to 157,474 in DE, and none contains another — so these are
# UNIONED, and an app is described by whichever of them will describe it.
# Both the enumeration and the description use this list, which is what keeps a game from
# being listed and then refused. Regenerate with
#   cargo run --release --features tools --bin steam_catalogue -- <out-dir> [how-many|all] [country]
# SORTED BY app_id, NUMERICALLY ASCENDING — 90 before 1000 — so the file can be binary-searched
# Any cell but app_id may be `?`, which means unknown to us and nothing else. A row of nothing
# but `?` is an app known only by its id; steam-delisted-games.tsv says which of those the
# store refuses, and steam-issues.tsv why any `?` was written
# An EMPTY list column (tagids, incl, feats, devs, pubs) means NONE, which is not the same
# as `?`. `?` is "not known"; empty is "known to be nothing". steam-issues.tsv records the
# cases where an empty list is itself suspect, such as a game with no tags at all
# type       Valve's own product kind: 0 game, 11 music. A games-only sweep is all 0s; widening
#            the search past category1=998 is what makes the column earn its place
# band       0-9, Valve's own `review_score`; 0 is "too few reviews to name a band".
#            Decode through steam-bands.tsv
# approval   percent of those reviews that are positive — the "% Positive" a store page prints
# reviews    how many reviews that percentage is over
#            band, approval and reviews all come from `summary_filtered`, whose population is
#            ALL LANGUAGES but `purchase_type=steam`. THAT DIFFERS FROM THE REST OF THIS
#            PROGRAM, which asks for `purchase_type=all` so that key-activated copies count —
#            the population a bundle catalogue cares about. Valve publishes no bulk summary
#            over it, so expect these three to disagree with the curated table in src/inventory
# released   YYYY-MM-DD out on that day; ~YYYY-MM-DD not out yet, planned for that day; TBA
#            not out yet, no date announced; X out, no date published; ? unknown — the item
#            service gave none and appdetails could not say (no-release-date), or the date
#            would not read (unreadable-release-date)
# os         a bit mask: 1 windows, 2 mac, 4 linux
# vr         1 when the store names any headset (Vive, Rift, Index, Windows MR or a generic HMD)
# early      1 when the store marks it Early Access
# deck       Steam Deck compatibility: 0 unknown, 1 unsupported, 2 playable, 3 verified
# compat     ONE base-64 digit (0-9A-Za-z+/) holding the three verdicts beside the Deck one, on
#            that same 0-3 scale: bits 0-1 SteamOS, bits 2-3 Steam Frame, bits 4-5 Steam Machine
# lang_*     base-36 64-bit masks over Valve's `elanguage`, where bit N is language N; 0 is a
#            store listing none, and `?` a list the masks cannot express. The three
#            are Valve's `supported`, `full_audio` and `subtitles` — the Interface, Full Audio
#            and Subtitles columns of the language table on a store page. Checked against
#            `appdetails` on app 620: both report 27 languages and the same 5 with full audio.
#            A row carrying ONLY an `eadditionallanguage` (a regional variant such as Spanish -
#            Latin America, elanguage -1) sets no bit; its base language keeps its own
# tagids     Valve's own numbers in base 36, resolved by steam-tags.tsv. IN VALVE'S OWN ORDER,
#            which is DESCENDING BY VOTE WEIGHT — the first tag is the strongest, not the
#            alphabetically first. Up to 20 per game
# incl       other apps Steam ties to this one through its store item, base 36. NOT a parent
#            pointer and NOT reliably mutual: app 10 and app 80 name each other, while app 620's
#            soundtrack names 620 and 620 names nothing. 7,158 of 30,000 games carry at least one
# feats      store feature ids in base 36, resolved by steam-categories.tsv: the checkboxes a
#            store page lists (Single-player, Co-op, Steam Cloud, Full controller support …).
#            Valve returns them as three arrays by kind; they are merged here and ascending,
#            because the kind belongs to the id and the sidecar already records it
# devs, pubs names joined by `;`, since a studio name can contain a comma
# Where the item service publishes nothing, a cell may carry a fact found elsewhere instead;
# every one is listed, with where it was seen, in steam-overrides.tsv
